articles.title: Harbaugh, McDaniel React to Justin Herbert, Chargers Being Tied for Worst Record in NFL Standings
articles.summary: Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh and offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel aren't reaching for the panic button after the team dropped its first two games of the 2026 NFL season.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh and offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel aren't reaching for the panic button after the team dropped its first two games of the 2026 NFL season.

Harbaugh told reporters earlier this week the team is experiencing some "growing pains" after having replaced both coordinators. Greg Roman was dismissed, and Jesse Minter, who led the defense, left to become the Baltimore Ravens' head coach.

McDaniel, for his part, said the Chargers are "not standing on business in the least," per ESPN's Kris Rhim .

The performance of the offense has been particularly disappointing. Los Angeles has already committed five turnovers, and franchise quarterback Justin Herbert has thrown for just 401 yards and two touchdowns while completing 59.3 percent of his passes.

"I think I can just plain and simply say that it's below our expectations," McDaniel said. "I know it's below a lot of people's expectations as well."

Making a splashy hire and adding McDaniel to the staff made plenty of sense. He brought the best out of Tua Tagovailoa and Tyreek Hill while coaching the Miami Dolphins. He was also a major departure from Roman in terms of his scheme and familiarity with Harbaugh.

Instead, a lot of the same problems from recent seasons are carrying over.

McDaniel said he isn't going to totally scrap his game plan but doesn't want to overreact.

"What I know how to do is evolve. And so I think it's kind of lazy to just say, 'OK, there's the result. Not good. Let's do the opposite,'" he said, per Rhim. "That's not why I'm here. That being said, you don't just point a finger and say, 'Well, it worked before.' So I think all of that is being taken under consideration."

Compounding the concern generated from the 0-2 start, the Chargers' schedule doesn't get any easier. They play the Buffalo Bills, Seattle Seahawks, Denver Broncos and Kansas City Chiefs before heading into a Week 7 bye.

Picking up a couple of wins over playoff contenders would definitely improve the general vibes around L.A. But such a difficult stretch could only serve to worsen the team's position in the standings and amplify the fans' frustrations.

articles.title: New Tyson Bagent Injury Update Revealed Ahead of Bears' Game vs. Eagles amid Caleb Williams' Injury
articles.summary: Caleb Williams' hamstring isn't the only injury the Chicago Bears have to worry about heading into their Week 3 game against the Philadelphia Eagles.
articles.body:
Caleb Williams' hamstring isn't the only injury the Chicago Bears have to worry about heading into their Week 3 game against the Philadelphia Eagles.

Backup quarterback Tyson Bagent is in the NFL's concussion protocol, which means third-stringer Case Keenum may be tasked with taking the field against the Eagles on Monday. However, Bagent has made progress and has yet to be ruled out, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter:

Schefter Talks Possible Giants QB Targets

Williams suffered the injury during Sunday's loss to the Minnesota Vikings, and Bagent entered the game in the fourth quarter with the team trailing.

He had an opportunity to win it, but the offense stalled ahead of a blocked field goal on his first possession. It then moved into the red zone in the final seconds trailing by six only for it to turn the ball over on downs on the final play of the 9-3 loss.

Still, having more than a week to prepare for the Eagles alongside head coach Ben Johnson figured to put Bagent in a better spot to succeed than when he was thrown into the fourth quarter of a divisional showdown in rainy conditions.

Yet those plans are apparently on hold as he is in concussion protocol, leaving Chicago's quarterback situation tenuous at best.

Keenum is a veteran who has 66 career starts during a career that includes stops with the Houston Texans, St. Louis/Los Angeles Rams, Vikings, Denver Broncos, Washington, Cleveland Browns and Buffalo Bills.

But he hasn't started a game since he went 1-1 during the 2023 campaign. Starting him against a playoff contender such as the Eagles was not in the cards for the Bears heading into the season.

Ultimately, Chicago's long-term outlook for the season depends on Williams' status. Johnson said he is considered "week-to-week," although Rapoport noted he will "likely" be out against Philadelphia.

If Bagent is out as well, the Bears will be staring at an uphill battle in their next game.

articles.title: Delhi SIR: Special camps on Sunday to enrol eligible voters
articles.summary: Delhi to hold special voter enrolment camps Sept 27 at all polling stations and Sept 29-30 at colleges to add missing names in SIR draft rolls.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Delhi election officials will hold special camps at all polling stations across 70 assembly constituencies Sunday to help eligible voters left out of the draft SIR roll apply for inclusion. Separate camps will be organised at colleges, universities and other educational institutions on Sept 29 and 30 to enrol gen-Z voters.The camps are part of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Delhi. The office of the chief electoral officer said the Sept27 exercise would be the second special camp for left-out eligible citizens, following the first one held on Sept 20.At Sunday’s polling station camps, eligible citizens whose names are missing from the draft electoral roll can approach booth-level officers (BLOs) for assistance in submitting form 6 for inclusion.The Sept 29-30 camps at educational institutions will focus on enrolling electors aged 18 to 25 years. BLOs will be present with electoral rolls and blank form 6 forms to guide eligible students through the application process.Those who have completed or will complete 18 years of age by Oct 1, 2026, and whose names are not in the draft electoral roll can apply for inclusion along with the required supporting documents.For new electors, form 6 requires proof of age and ordinary residence. Accepted age-proof documents include a birth certificate, Aadhaar card, PAN card, driving licence, Class X or XII certificate and passport. Residence can be established through documents such as Aadhaar card, utility bills, bank or post office passbook, passport, land records, registered rent agreement or registered sale deed.Applicants must also submit the prescribed declaration form, which seeks details of the applicant and their linkage with the electoral roll of the last SIR, including details of specified relatives and their EPIC numbers, where available.Forms 6, 6A, 7 and 8 can also be submitted at the camps. Form 6 is for inclusion of new voters; form 6A is for inclusion of overseas electors; form 7 is for objections to the proposed inclusion or deletion of a name; and form 8 is for shifting of residence, correction of entries, replacement of EPIC or marking of PwD.BLOs will be available at the camps to assist electors with the filing process.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Lions' Amon-Ra St. Brown Hit with Steep Fine by NFL for 4 Unsportsmanlike Conduct Infractions
articles.summary: Amon-Ra St. Brown will have to fork over almost $60,000 to the NFL for his celebrations during the Lions' loss last Thursday to the Buffalo Bills.
articles.body:
Amon-Ra St. Brown will have to fork over almost $60,000 to the NFL for his celebrations during the Lions' loss last Thursday to the Buffalo Bills.

The NFL announced Saturday St. Brown was fined $59,704 after being assessed four unsportsmanlike conduct violations for "illegal celebrations and vulgar acts" at the cost of $14,926 each.

St. Brown told reporters Thursday he intended to appeal the NFL's decision.

"It's not good, man. 14 something times four, you do the math," St. Brown said Thursday (h/t Nolan Dianchi of the Detroit News . "But I'm gonna appeal it."

St. Brown wasn't the only Lions player left with a bill after the loss to the Bills. Jameson Williams, Penei Sewell and Jahmyr Gibbs were each hit with $14,926 fines for an illegal celebration.

Williams also picked up a $11,941 fine for taunting, while Tyler Lacy and Devin White were charged more than $7,000 each for facemask violations.

One of the celebrations for which St. Brown was penalized took place after he caught a touchdown pass from Jared Goff to start out last Thursday's second half by cutting the Bills' lead to 10 points.

The Lions were unable to close the deficit further before conceding the 41-31 loss, during which St. Brown recorded nine catches on 13 targets for 142 yards and two touchdowns.

St. Brown isn't the only player who has pushed back against the NFL's decision to fine players for imitating smoking or drinking in on-field celebrations.

San Francisco 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk argued against a Week 2 fines for a celebration in which he mimicked chugging a drink he said represented juice.

Bud Light, an NFL sponsor, has leaned into the discussion by keeping track of how many fines players have racked up for drinking-related celebrations so far this season.

articles.title: $58 Million Former Houston Texans Free Agency Bust Joins Green Bay Packers
articles.summary: The Houston Texans could square off against former free agent pickup and starter Laken Tomlinson following his latest deal. The post $58 Million Former Houst...
articles.body:
The Houston Texans could see old friend and starting left guard Laken Tomlinson down the road this regular season.

"Long-time NFL guard Laken Tomlinson is being signed by the # Packers off the #Cowboys practice squad, per me and @MikeGarafolo," NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported in a post on X on September 26.

"At age 34, with 162 starts under his belt, Tomlinson will help an O-line that needs it."

It is a quick turn for Tomlinson, who started seven of 10 games for the Texans in 2025 after signing with the organization in free agency that spring.

Tomlinson, 34, has earned more than $58 million in his career so far.

Packers Poach Former Texans Starter From Cowboys

"The #Packers make a move for a veteran to help their offensive line," NFL Network's Mike Garafolo posted in reaction. "Tomlinson signed with the #Cowboys a few weeks ago, now headed to Green Bay ."

The Packers are coming off a deflating loss at home to the Atlanta Falcons in Week 2.

However, this deal also sets up a potential revenge opportunity for Tomlinson. The Packers and Texans will face off in Green Bay in Week 17 of the regular season.

The Texans moved on from Tomlinson during the 2025 campaign, but their offensive line remains unsettled. Whether that says more about him or them remains to be seen. However, he was with the Baltimore Ravens to end the 2025 season.

Not only did they allow him to walk, but the Cowboys only had him on their practice squad.

This is undoubtedly a significant opportunity for Tomlinson. It does, however, bring into question just how uncertain the Packers are about their offensive line two weeks into the season.

That is an encouraging footnote for a Texans defense that is still trying to find its elite form from recent seasons, albeit one that will not matter until later in the season, by which time both team's could be in vastly different situation than they find themselves in now.

articles.title: Chris Olave draws same fine for taunting as uncalled Ravens facemask
articles.summary: The NFL issued matching fines to Saints wide receiver Chris Olave and Ravens linebacker Roquan Smith, but only one of them drew a penalty flag.
articles.body:
New Orleans Saints wide receiver Chris Olave and Baltimore Ravens linebacker Roquan Smith received fines from last week's game between the two teams. Each player was fined for separate incidents during the Saints 24-17 victory at Baltimore. The NFL announced the decisions on Saturday.

Olave was fined $11,941 for taunting/unsportsman behavior towards Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey . That infraction happened on a 20-yard completion from quarterback Tyler Shough to Olave down the left sideline against Humphrey late in the first quarter of last week's game. The play picked up a first down into Ravens territory. However, Olave was penalized for unsportsmanlike conduct (taunting), pushing New Orleans back 15 yards. NFL insider Tom Pelissero observed that the Olave fine was one of 22 issued by the league last week for obscene gestures or illegal celebrations.

Smith was fined $11,941 for a face mask infraction on Saints quarterback Tyler Shough. That happened with 1:32 left in the fourth quarter on a quarterback sneak by Shough, resulting in a touchdown that would give New Orleans a 24-17 lead. The play was reviewed and upheld by replay. Shough's head was twisted backwards during the run, but Smith was not penalized on the play.

articles.title: Seahawks star JSN ranked high in ESPN’s fantasy football rankings
articles.summary: Seahawks star Jaxon Smith-Njigba is forecasted to be among the top producers in fantasy football for the rest of the season.
articles.body:
Seattle Seahawks star Jaxon Smith-Njigba is on track to top all wide receivers in the NFL in fantasy football this season.

ESPN's Eric Karabell ranked Smith-Njigba No. 1 overall among all wide receivers in the NFL and No. 2 overall among all players in his rest-of-season fantasy football rankings following the Seahawks superstar's explosive start to the year.

Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs is the only player ranked ahead of Smith-Njigba in the overall player rankings.

Smith-Njigba has totaled 17 receptions for 277 receiving yards and four touchdowns through two games. He opened the season with eight catches for 122 yards and a touchdown against the New England Patriots , then produced nine receptions for 155 yards and three touchdowns in Seattle's 31-7 victory over the Arizona Cardinals . Smith-Njigba leads the league in receiving yards and touchdowns at the present.

Seattle's upcoming schedule will test Smith-Njigba against stronger competition, but his high target share, ability to create explosive gains and central role in the team's offense make him an elite WR1. His reception and yardage volume provide a stable foundation for continued success in fantasy football moving forward. Smith-Njigba has scored the most fantasy points among all wide receivers in ESPN points per reception leagues thus far with 68.7.

articles.title: FAMU football QB Armond Parker starting vs Alabama A&M in SWAC opener
articles.summary: True freshman Armond Parker starts at quarterback for Florida A&M against Alabama A&M after recent injuries.
articles.body:
Per the team-provided depth chart to the media, the true freshman is starting at quarterback for the Rattlers in Saturday's Southwestern Athletic Conference opener on Ken Riley Field at Bragg Memorial Stadium . James Hayes is the backup, and Dustin Fletcher , last week's starter, isn't listed.

The Locust Grove, Georgia, native is the Rattlers' third starting quarterback of the season as injuries have caused a carousel at the position. He opened the season as the third string.

FAMU football hosts Tennessee State in HBCU matchup | Our top photos

At quarterback last week against Tennessee State , Fletcher hurt his thumb in the second quarter while replacing original starter Isaiah Knowles, who had a season-ending thumb injury . At his exit, Fletcher was 6-for-11 passing for 48 yards, threw a touchdown, and rushed for 28 yards. He was on track for a good performance before being forced to leave the game. When the Tallahassee Democrat attended FAMU's Wednesday practice , Fletcher was dressed in his jersey and shorts, but not practicing.

Parker checked in the Tennessee State game and completed 14 of 25 pass attempts for 267 yards, threw two touchdowns, and tossed a 61-yard pick-six in the 29-26 loss for the Rattlers . Fresh out of high school, he proved he was capable of running head coach Quinn Fordham Gray Sr.'s offense and built on his Most Improved Player award during spring football camp this April.

FAMU-Alabama A&M is being televised on SWAC TV and kicks off at 7 p.m. 96.1 JAMZ will also have radio commentary by FAMU Hall of Fame quarterback Albert Chester and school alumnus Bryan Fulford.

articles.title: "She was done": Gisele Bündchen’s heartbreaking realization reportedly ended her marriage to Tom Brady
articles.summary: Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen’s marriage looked glamorous from the outside, but a new biography claims the relationship faced deep tension behind the
articles.body: Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen’s marriage looked glamorous from the outside, but a new biography claims the relationship faced deep tension behind the scenes. The former couple, who married in 2009 and divorced in 2022, had built a family while Brady continued pursuing an NFL career that demanded much of his time and attention. According to Lars Anderson’s upcoming book, Brady: An American Story and the Price of Greatness, Bündchen ultimately decided to end the marriage. The account offers a new perspective on the pressures that reportedly shaped their relationship, particularly as Brady continued playing long after Bündchen hoped he would step away.Gisele Bündchen and Tom Brady faced growing marriage tensionAccording to an excerpt from Anderson’s biography published by the Daily Mail, the end of Brady and Bündchen’s marriage was linked to differences over their future.The book claims Bündchen had wanted Brady to retire from football earlier, with Anderson pointing to 2017 as a period when she hoped he might leave the sport. Even after the Patriots won another Super Bowl in 2019, the issue reportedly remained unresolved.Bündchen allegedly asked Brady, “Would now be the perfect time to retire?”Brady’s reported response showed just how differently they viewed his career at the time: “Too bad, babe. I’m having too much fun right now.”“One day, Gisele, who is really into astrology, basically looked into the stars and told Tom, ‘We’re not compatible,’ and just like that, she was done,” reads an excerpt published in the Daily Mail.Football was not the only source of tension described in the book. Anderson also portrays Bündchen as wanting greater involvement from Brady at home, particularly with their children.The biography claims she wanted him to be more present when he was away from the football environment and have more time available for family life and her own career.Tom Brady’s NFL career shaped their relationshipBrady’s commitment to football remained a defining part of his life. After nearly two decades with the New England Patriots, he moved to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2020 and won another Super Bowl during his first season with the team.The book’s account suggests that his extraordinary career came with personal costs. A friend of Brady’s reportedly described a lifestyle dominated by strict routines, training, games and constant preparation.“The whole lifestyle had to be getting tiresome for Gisele,” the source said, according to Anderson.Brady eventually announced his retirement in 2023, after briefly stepping away from football and returning for another season.The former couple now share two children, Vivian and Benjamin. Brady also has a son, Jack, from his previous relationship with Bridget Moynahan.Bündchen has since entered a new chapter of her life. She married Joaquim Valente in 2025, and the couple welcomed their first child that same year.While the biography presents one account of what happened inside Brady and Bündchen’s marriage, the former couple have largely kept the most personal details of their split private. articles.title: Travis Kelce paid $6 million for a 17,000-square-foot Kansas mansion, scoring it for $900,000 below asking and adding a private underground golf simulator
articles.summary: Travis Kelce’s $6 million Kansas mansion was more than another luxury purchase for an NFL superstar.
articles.body: Travis Kelce’s $6 million Kansas mansion was more than another luxury purchase for an NFL superstar. The sprawling Leawood property arrived at a moment when his life was changing at remarkable speed. In 2023, as attention around his relationship with Taylor Swift exploded, Kelce moved from a relatively modest Kansas City home to a gated estate designed around privacy, space and entertainment. The 17,000-square-foot property came with a pool, sports courts, a miniature golf course and plenty of room to disappear from the spotlight. He later took the home a step further by adding plans for a private underground golf simulator.Travis Kelce’s $6 million mansion was bought for privacyWhen Kelce purchased the Leawood property, the move quickly became one of the most talked-about celebrity real estate stories in Kansas City.The timing was impossible to ignore. Kelce had become one of the NFL’s biggest stars, while his relationship with Swift had suddenly placed his private life under a level of attention that few professional athletes experience.The Los Angeles Times reported that Kelce bought the mansion for about $6 million, with privacy concerns surrounding the move. His previous Kansas City-area home had reportedly become a destination for fans and photographers after his romance with Swift became public.The new property offered a very different setting.Located in a gated community in Leawood, Kansas, the estate sits on nearly 3.5 acres at the end of a quiet cul-de-sac. Realtor.com reported that the property had originally been listed for $6.9 million, meaning Kelce secured it for roughly $900,000 below the asking price.That discount makes the purchase even more interesting. Kelce was not simply paying for square footage. He was buying distance from the public.And there was plenty of space to justify the price.Inside Travis Kelce’s sprawling Leawood estateThe mansion stretches across roughly 17,000 square feet and includes six bedrooms and six bathrooms. It was built in 1998 and sits behind a gated entrance that leads to a large circular driveway.Inside, the home has the kind of spaces expected from a property built for entertaining. There is a chef’s kitchen, formal dining room, media lounge, wine cellar and full bar.The outdoor area is arguably even more impressive.The backyard includes what has been described as a “Beverly Hills-style” pool area, complete with a waterfall. There is also an outdoor kitchen, hot tub, tennis and pickleball court and miniature golf course. A six-car garage adds another layer of convenience to the estate.For an NFL player, the sporting features make particular sense. Kelce spends much of his life around competition, training and team facilities. At home, he has a property that can keep him active without leaving the estate.But the mansion is not all about football.Its entertainment spaces, landscaped grounds and secluded location make it suitable for hosting family and friends while keeping much of that activity away from public view.That privacy became even more relevant as Kelce’s profile grew.Travis Kelce added an underground golf simulatorKelce did not leave the $6 million property untouched.In 2024, reports revealed plans for a new underground space beneath the mansion. Realtor.com reported that the project involved a roughly 396-square-foot area designed to include a golf simulator. Construction plans called for the existing basement floor to be lowered by about two feet to create additional room.The city of Leawood confirmed that a permit had been filed for work involving the existing basement, drainage and concrete walls, according to Realtor.com.It is a small addition compared with the size of the overall estate, but it says plenty about how Kelce uses the property.A golf simulator gives him a private way to work on his game without dealing with crowds or travel. Kelce has also played celebrity golf alongside his brother Jason and other stars, making the addition feel less like a random luxury and more like an extension of one of his hobbies.The project also fits into a broader luxury-home trend sometimes called an “iceberg house,” where owners build downward to create additional private space without dramatically changing the exterior. Realtor.com described Kelce’s project as part of that growing trend.For Kelce, however, the appeal appears especially practical. The mansion already has extensive outdoor amenities, so adding another recreational space underground gives him something different without taking away from the property’s existing character.The mansion became part of Travis Kelce’s personal storyThe Leawood mansion eventually became more than a place to live.In 2025, it became closely linked to one of the biggest moments in Kelce’s personal life when he proposed to Swift at the property. Realtor.com reported that the proposal took place at the Kansas home, while Architectural Digest described the backyard as the setting for the engagement moment.That detail gives the property a significance that goes well beyond its price tag.The home was originally chosen at a time when Kelce needed more privacy. Yet it later became the backdrop for an intensely personal moment that attracted worldwide attention.The estate also reflects how Kelce’s life has evolved since his NFL career made him a household name. He still owns his earlier Kansas City-area property, which he bought for $995,000 in 2019, according to Realtor.com.But the Leawood mansion represents a different level of luxury.It has the scale for entertaining, the security of a gated setting and enough private recreation to keep its owner occupied without stepping outside. Most importantly, it gave Kelce something his earlier home could no longer provide as his fame grew: separation.The $6 million purchase therefore tells a bigger story than the price alone. Kelce bought a mansion, but he also bought privacy, space and control over his surroundings. Then he kept reshaping the property to fit his lifestyle.From the sprawling pool and sports courts to the underground golf simulator, the Leawood estate has become a private extension of the NFL star’s world. articles.title: NFL no Maracanã: entenda a partida e adaptações no estádio | G1
articles.standfirst: Dallas Cowboys e Baltimore Ravens se enfrentam neste domingo (27), no primeiro jogo da liga no estádio; veja como o palco do futebol foi preparado para receber o futebol americano.
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys e Baltimore Ravens se enfrentam neste domingo (27), no primeiro jogo da liga no estádio; veja como o palco do futebol foi preparado para receber o futebol americano.
articles.body:
O Maracanã vai trocar, por um dia, o futebol pela bola oval. Neste domingo (27), o estádio recebe pela primeira vez uma partida da NFL, a principal liga de futebol americano dos Estados Unidos. Dallas Cowboys e Baltimore Ravens se enfrentam às 17h25, em duelo válido pela terceira semana da temporada regular.

O Globo Comunidade deste domingo recebeu Kiko Menezes, que explicou como funciona o esporte e como o estádio mais famoso do Brasil se preparou para receber o duelo.

Para receber a partida, o tradicional estádio do futebol brasileiro passou por uma série de adaptações. A NFL começou a planejar as mudanças com cerca de um ano de antecedência, enviando profissionais ao Rio para mapear a estrutura necessária para o evento.

As alterações vão muito além da pintura das linhas no gramado. Os vestiários ganharam mais chuveiros e armários temporários, foram criados espaços adicionais para guardar equipamentos e o campo foi adaptado às dimensões e às áreas de segurança exigidas pelo futebol americano.

Isso acontece porque a estrutura necessária para uma partida de NFL é bem diferente daquela usada em um jogo de futebol.

Cada equipe da liga tem 53 jogadores no elenco ativo, além de atletas do practice squad. A quantidade de equipamentos também é muito maior. No futebol, uma equipe costuma relacionar 23 jogadores para uma partida.

Campo do Maracanã ganhou marcações para receber jogo da NFL — Foto: Reprodução/ TV Globo

A transformação mais visível acontece no gramado. As linhas tradicionais do futebol dão lugar às marcações de jardas características da NFL, e as traves em formato de “Y” são instaladas atrás das end zones.

O campo de futebol americano tem 120 jardas de comprimento, incluindo as duas end zones, e 53,3 jardas de largura. A área central entre as end zones possui 100 jardas.

No Maracanã, as delimitações foram adaptadas, com o campo ficando mais estreito nas laterais e mais alongado nas extremidades para atender às especificações do esporte.

A NFL também ampliou as áreas de escape ao redor do campo. A medida é uma questão de segurança para os jogadores, que realizam jogadas de alta velocidade e contato físico intenso.

Maracanã recebe, neste domingo (27), jogo da NFL — Foto: Reprodução/ TV Globo

O confronto reúne duas franquias tradicionais da NFL.

O Dallas Cowboys é um dos times mais conhecidos da liga e conquistou cinco títulos do Super Bowl. A equipe é conhecida nos Estados Unidos pelo apelido de “America's Team”.

O Baltimore Ravens tem dois títulos do Super Bowl e chega ao Rio com o quarterback Lamar Jackson como uma de suas principais atrações.

Jackson é conhecido pela capacidade de lançar a bola e também pela habilidade para correr. Do lado dos Cowboys, o quarterback é Dak Prescott.

O jogo marca a estreia da NFL no Rio de Janeiro . Nas duas temporadas anteriores, a liga realizou partidas no Brasil na Neo Química Arena, em São Paulo.

A Companhia de Engenharia de Tráfego do Rio de Janeiro (CET-Rio) irá implantar uma operação especial de trânsito no entorno do Estádio do Maracanã, na Zona Norte. O planejamento prevê a proibição de estacionamento, bloqueios viários em etapas e organização do acesso de táxis e veículos de aplicativo.

A partida está prevista para começar às 17h25, com abertura dos portões às 13h. As restrições ao estacionamento terão início às 19h de sábado (26/09), enquanto os bloqueios de trânsito serão implantados em etapas, a partir das 10h de domingo, sete horas antes do início do jogo. As vias serão liberadas ao tráfego de veículos até as 23h, após duas horas do fim da partida.

Às 11h, será implantado o bloqueio total do entorno, incluindo a Avenida Rei Pelé, no sentido Méier. Durante essa etapa, o trânsito será desviado pela Rua Ceará, para os motoristas que seguem em direção ao Méier, e pela Rua Mariz e Barros, para quem trafega no sentido Tijuca.

A operação contará com 205 operadores e agentes de trânsito, 26 painéis de mensagens variáveis, 25 motocicletas, 12 viaturas e três reboques. O efetivo atuará no monitoramento do trânsito, na orientação aos motoristas e na implantação dos bloqueios e desvios necessários.

A CET-Rio recomenda que o uso do transporte público para chegar e sair do estádio. Motoristas devem antecipar seus deslocamentos, manter atenção à sinalização e às orientações dos agentes de trânsito e evitar circular pelas vias do entorno durante a implantação dos bloqueios.

Esquema especial de funcionamento do MetrôRio

O MetrôRio preparou um esquema especial para o próximo domingo (27/09). O metrô é a melhor opção de transporte para chegar ao evento. A concessionária vai ampliar a oferta de trens durante a chegada ao estádio e a dispersão do público, além de reforçar o efetivo de segurança e de operadores de estação. Haverá estruturas de controle de fluxo nas estações mais próximas ao estádio.

No domingo (27/09), o sistema metroviário funcionará das 7h às 23h. As linhas 1 e 4 operarão no trecho entre Uruguai e Jardim Oceânico/Barra da Tijuca, enquanto a Linha 2 funcionará entre Pavuna e General Osório/Ipanema. A transferência entre as linhas 1 e 2 poderá ser realizada no trecho entre as estações Central do Brasil e General Osório.

Diego Haidar e Kiko Menezes mostram como funciona o futebol americano — Foto: Reprodução

Para quem está acostumado ao futebol, a lógica pode parecer complicada. Mas a ideia central é simples: avançar pelo campo e chegar à end zone adversária.

Cada equipe coloca 11 jogadores em campo por vez. Um time fica no ataque e o outro na defesa.

O time que está atacando tem quatro tentativas, chamadas de downs, para avançar pelo menos 10 jardas.

Se conseguir, ganha uma nova sequência de quatro tentativas para avançar outras 10 jardas.

Por exemplo: se uma equipe avançar quatro jardas na primeira jogada, três na segunda e quatro na terceira, terá percorrido 11 jardas e conquistado uma nova primeira descida.

Se não conseguir atingir as 10 jardas nas quatro tentativas, normalmente perde a posse da bola.

A principal forma de marcar no futebol americano é o touchdown. Ele acontece quando um jogador entra na end zone com a bola ou recebe um passe dentro da área. O touchdown vale seis pontos.

Depois da pontuação, a equipe ainda pode marcar pontos extras. Um chute entre as traves vale um ponto. Também existe a possibilidade de tentar uma jogada para marcar dois pontos.

Outra forma de pontuar é o field goal. Quando o chute passa entre as traves em formato de “Y”, a equipe marca três pontos.

O quarterback é uma das posições mais conhecidas do futebol americano. Ele recebe a bola no início da jogada e pode decidir o que fazer: lançar um passe, entregar a bola para um companheiro correr ou, em determinadas situações, correr com ela.

É também um dos principais responsáveis por interpretar a defesa adversária e executar a estratégia definida pela comissão técnica.

No Maracanã, os olhos estarão especialmente voltados para Lamar Jackson, dos Ravens, e Dak Prescott, dos Cowboys.

Outra diferença importante em relação ao futebol é a especialização das equipes.

Os jogadores de ataque entram em campo quando o time possui a bola. Quando a posse muda, a unidade defensiva assume a função de tentar impedir o avanço adversário.

Também existem equipes especiais, responsáveis principalmente por jogadas como chutes e retornos.

Por que os jogadores usam tantos equipamentos?

Proteção interna de capacete da NFL — Foto: Reprodução/ TV Globo

O futebol americano é um esporte de contato e envolve colisões em alta velocidade. Por isso, os jogadores utilizam capacete, proteção para os ombros e outros equipamentos.

O capacete possui uma estrutura externa rígida e materiais internos para ajudar a absorver os impactos. Alguns atletas também usam uma proteção adicional sobre o capacete, aumentando a camada externa de proteção.

A proteção facial é outro componente importante. Alguns jogadores utilizam ainda viseiras acopladas ao capacete.

Mesmo com os equipamentos, existem regras específicas para limitar determinados tipos de contato e proteger os atletas.

A partida é dividida em quatro períodos de 15 minutos, totalizando 60 minutos de tempo regulamentar.

Na prática, porém, um jogo de NFL costuma durar bem mais de uma hora. O relógio é interrompido em diversas situações, como passes incompletos, saídas de campo, pedidos de tempo e revisões de jogadas.

articles.title: 3 takeaways from Utah’s road victory at Iowa State
articles.summary: Facing their first adversity of the season, the Utes responded well and sealed the road victory
articles.body:
The way Utah played in the first half against Iowa State Saturday, you might have thought the game would end the same way the Utes ' first three games of the season did, with a big Utah win.

But the Cyclones didn't go down quietly.

Down 24-3 at halftime, Jimmy Rogers' staff made the right adjustments against a physical and swarming Ute defense. Keeping the ball in the hands of quarterback Jaylen Raynor and controlling time of possession, Iowa State cut the deficit to 24-17 with 10:48 to play.

However, trusting running back Wayshawn Parker , the Utes had one more touchdown drive in them and eventually put the Cyclones away 31-17.

Coming into the game, some thought wet field conditions might slow down Utah's rushing attack and allow Iowa State to keep the game close.

It was almost as if Parker took offense to that narrative, because on the first snap of the game he took it directly for a 54-yard run to the house, outrunning the two defenders who had a half-chance to take him down.

The junior running back had two touchdowns and 92 of the Utes' 112 rushing yards in the first half.

Parker ended with 239 total yards — 174 rushing and 65 receiving — and three touchdowns, two rushing and one receiving.

But outside of No. 1, Utah struggled to get much going on the ground. Quarterback Devon Dampier was the Utes' second-leading rusher but put up just 16 rushing yards against the Cyclones.

That was uncharacteristic of the QB, who usually flashes his dual threat abilities and gives nightmares to opposing coaches, but Parker's stellar performance was enough to carry Utah to the finish line.

When Iowa State scored its first three points of the game in the first half, it was largely thanks to Utah's defensive line lining up offside to stop the quarterback sneak on a fourth and 1.

On another two sequences, the Cyclones were gifted a pass interference penalties that helped Iowa State score two touchdowns.

Utes head coach Morgan Scalley was not happy postgame with these unnecessary penalties that caused his team to shoot itself in the foot. While Utah still came away with the victory, it is an area Scalley will surely address before his squad goes up against a more formidable foe.

Utah faced adversity for the first time this season — and was up to the challenge

After halftime when the score was 24-3, it appeared Utah would come out in the second half to put the Cyclones under.

On one hand, the Utes did bend in allowing Iowa State to get within just a touchdown, but on a more positive note, Utah didn't break in both its first road game and its first Big 12 game of the season.

But credit to Dampier, he was able to find his rhythm once again and feed the right players, namely Parker, to lift his team at the end by managing one more touchdown score to bury the Cyclones.

articles.title: Nick Sirianni explains his trust in Jalen Hurts as Eagles quarterback
articles.summary: Nick Sirianni recently discussed the immense responsibility that comes with playing QB and why he couldn't ask for a better partner than Jalen Hurts.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles ask a lot from Jalen Hurts. He's responsible for directing an offense, making split-second decisions under pressure, meeting the expectations of a passionate fan base, and serving as one of the organization's primary faces.

Those responsibilities only grow when expectations are as high as they are in Philadelphia. Head coach Nick Sirianni was asked about that responsibility on Saturday .

But let's rewind to a comment Hurts made. After last week's win over the Tennessee Titans , Hurts said he couldn't adequately put into words the responsibility that comes with playing quarterback in the NFL. As it turns out, Sirianni found that task just as difficult.

"It's hard work. I'm not sure I can either. It's a lot of hard work. It's a lot of responsibility. It's a lot of credit, and it's a lot of blame. It takes great mental toughness to be able to sustain the ups and downs that all these players go through on a weekly basis."

Coach Sirianni didn't just offer a simple explanation of the position. Instead, he expanded on why the quarterback role differs from any other in sports.

Nick Sirianni couldn't ask for a better partner than Jalen Hurts.

"I'm not sure I could put it into words, but there is immense responsibility to an organization and to a city in playing the most important position in sports. I'm sure glad we have Jalen Hurts playing the most important position in sports in Philadelphia because I love him and everything that he's done for us and everything he'll continue to do for us."

That statement naturally led Sirianni to discuss the player currently carrying that responsibility for the Eagles. The head coach has repeatedly praised Hurts throughout their time together. Still, his comments Saturday felt especially revealing because he made them while discussing leadership, accountability, and the pressure that comes with the position. Sirianni then compared his relationship with Hurts to one of the most important working partnerships inside the organization.

"I'm sure glad we have Jalen Hurts playing the most important position in sports in Philadelphia because I love him and everything that he's done for us and everything he'll continue to do for us. I always say about [Executive Vice President/General Manager] Howie [Roseman], I couldn't ask for a better partner in this and I feel the same way about Jalen. I couldn't ask for a better partner in this journey."

Those comments reflect the level of trust the Eagles continue to place in their quarterback. Hurts has already delivered his share of memorable moments through the first two weeks of the season, including helping guide Philadelphia through a dramatic victory over the Tennessee Titans .

While statistics and highlight plays often dominate conversations about quarterbacks, Sirianni's answer reminded everyone that leadership remains one of the qualities the organization values most. When discussing the immense responsibility that comes with being the quarterback of the Philadelphia Eagles , Sirianni made one thing abundantly clear: no one would rather have Jalen Hurts carrying that burden or battling with him in the foxhole.

articles.title: GM Jon-Eric Sullivan looking at tough decision if Dolphins pick No. 1
articles.summary: The Dolphins are 0-2 through two weeks and appear headed to the top pick in the 2027 NFL Draft, where they would have a very tough decision to make.
articles.body:
When the 2026 NFL regular season comes to a close in January, the Miami Dolphins could very well own the number one overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. According to ESPN, the odds that Miami will possess that first pick are a whopping 46% as of Saturday heading into Week 3.

While that may be the smart money to predict, what is not at this moment is which player general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan could select. Of course, he may elect to trade out and acquire a treasure chest of draft assets, but let's put a pin in that for now.

Sullivan was in attendance for the Texas and Tennessee game on Saturday at Neyland Stadium, and two Longhorns most likely had the majority of his attention. Quarterback Arch Manning and defensive end Colin Simmons are both potential top-five picks in 2027, but it may not be that simple to state.

Manning could elect to return to college, as some say he still needs a bit more time to develop. Depending on who you ask, others see him as the sure-fire top pick this coming April.

Manning and the No. 1-ranked Longhorns defeated No. 14 Tennessee 20-17, but it was Simmons who was the headliner. The pass-rusher registered a program-record five sacks, and his overall stat line was a ridiculous eight tackles (four for loss), a quarterback hit and a forced fumble. As for Manning, he threw for 201 yards and completed 14 of his 19 passes with no touchdowns and an interception.

That interception was a questionable throw, as Manning heaved the ball deep into clear double coverage. Pundits across college football and social media have varying evaluations of Manning, and at this exact time, he doesn't seem to be the consensus top selection when April rolls around.

Adding more intrigue to the debate on who Miami, or whichever team holds the 2027 No. 1 pick, should take, a generational talent at wide receiver had a monster day in Columbus, Ohio, Saturday. Jeremiah Smith had an incredible performance for the Buckeyes with a triple-crown of career highs, catching 12 balls for 217 yards and four touchdowns. Additionally, Smith became the lone Ohio State receiver to eclipse 3,000 receiving yards, a program that is known as one of the best in producing talent at the position.

Circling back to the No. 1 pick debate, in NFL Draft history, just three receivers have been the top selection. The first was in 1964 when the San Francisco 49ers selected Dave Parks; then 20 years later in 1984, the New England Patriots drafted Irving Fryar at the top spot. The last wide receiver to be selected first was Keyshawn Johnson with the New York Jets in 1996.

As for defensive ends, back in 2000, Courtney Brown kicked off the 21 st century of drafts as the No. 1 pick with the Cleveland Browns . It was the first time since 1992 that a defensive end was taken first when Steve Emtman was drafted by the Indianapolis Colts . Prior to Emtman, in 1984, a defensive end was selected first when the Buffalo Bills called Bruce Smith's name. Defensive ends at number one were a lot more common in the 60s and 70s, with names like Bubba Smith in 1967, Walt Patulski in 1972, John Matuszak in 1973, Too Tall Jones in 1974, and Lee Roy Selmon in 1976.

Back to the 2000s, following Brown, who had an underwhelming career for Cleveland in his five years there and one in Denver , just four defensive ends were the top pick since. Mario Williams in 2006, Jadeveon Clowney in 2014, Myles Garrett in 2017, and most recently Travon Walker in 2022.

Also, throughout the 2000s, there have been several busts at quarterback at No. 1. It's not a certainty the top signal-caller selected will prove to be a good investment for a team, or even remain on it. Failed picks for teams the last 25 years have included David Carr with the Houston Texans in 2002, JaMarcus Russell in 2007 with the Oakland Raiders, Sam Bradford with the St. Louis Rams in 2010, and Jameis Winston in 2015 with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers .

Then you have examples of quarterbacks who did not work out with their drafted teams yet went elsewhere, such as Baker Mayfield , when the Cleveland Browns took him in 2018, as well as Jared Goff ( Los Angeles Rams in 2016 and Matthew Stafford ( Detroit Lions in 2009), being part of a trade in 2021 for each other. Alex Smith with San Francisco from 2005 is another example. He spent seven seasons with the 49ers, but became a three-time Pro Bowler with the Chiefs in his five seasons with Kansas City .

And famously, in 2004, San Diego selected Eli Manning No. 1, but he was traded to the New York Giants in a deal that netted the Chargers Philip Rivers and a trio of additional draft picks. This was a situation where the Manning family called an audible, so to speak, after the Chargers called his name. That could very well happen again to some extent with Arch, should the team that gets the No. 1 pick is, let's say, undesirable to the family.

If Miami holds that No. 1 pick, in a pivotal second year in yet another rebuild, Sullivan will have the unenviable task of needing to hit a home run with his decision. As it stands now, from a player standpoint, Smith, Collins, or Manning seem like the consensus names at the top of the list.

Yet with all the needs Miami has on both sides of the ball, Sullivan could shop the pick or receive an offer he simply can't refuse. Moving a slot down or two could still net Miami Collins or Smith, and the 2026 play of current quarterback Malik Willis could influence that option. However, Willis has not proven just yet that he is, or isn't, the franchise quarterback for this team.

Also part of the equation in a potential trade-down, moving out of the top-five could mean missing on all three. This could be a cardinal sin in passing on talent, which consistently plagued Miami's previous general managers.

While the 2026 season in both college and the pros still has a long way to go, Sullivan and the Dolphins are in a position to be at the top of the board come April. If so, it would be just the third time in franchise history that Miami will own that top pick, the last being in 2008 when they picked tackle Jake Long over quarterback Matt Ryan , who went two picks later to the Atlanta Falcons . The first time they picked at the top was in 1966, their first year in existence.

Sullivan's decision, should he be the first man to make a pick, is one that could put Miami on the fast track to consistent success. But the wrong choice could derail any chance of his regime being the infrastructure to finally turn Miami's fortunes around. An organization that is still searching for its first playoff win since the 2000 season, its first Super Bowl appearance since the 1984 season, and its first championship since its back-to-back Lombardi Trophies in 1972 and 1973.

articles.title: Oregon QB Dante Moore leaves field on cart, in neck brace after late hit from USC’s Desman Stephens
articles.summary: Oregon quarterback Dante Moore left the Coliseum field on a stretcher in an ambulance while wearing a neck brace after the Heisman Trophy candidate was hit roughly by Southern California linebacker Desman Stephens during a slide in the second quarter Saturday.
articles.body: Oregon quarterback Dante Moore left the Coliseum field on a stretcher in an ambulance while wearing a neck brace after the Heisman Trophy candidate was hit roughly by Southern California linebacker Desman Stephens during a slide in the second quarter Saturday. Stephens’ hit resulted in his ejection for targeting and sparked a melee on the field while Moore was receiving immediate medical attention. The Ducks quarterback is an expected high pick in the next NFL draft. Moore was sliding to complete an 11-yard run to the USC 12 when Stephens came in low and hit Moore in the head and chest with his shoulder. Moore’s head snapped back and hit the turf hard, and his teammates immediately went after Stephens in a prolonged exchange. Both teams received unsportsmanlike conduct penalties. The No. 20 Ducks’ Big Ten opener against the 12th-ranked Trojans was delayed for about 15 minutes while Moore was cautiously treated and removed from the field on a cart. His teammates gathered around the cart to offer condolences and support before it was driven a few feet to a waiting ambulance at the base of the Coliseum tunnel. Moore could be seen moving both of his hands while strapped to the stretcher that was loaded into the ambulance. Coach Dan Lanning told NBC that Moore had movement in his extremities. Moore returned to Oregon for the current season despite the likely possibility of being a high pick in the NFL draft last April. Stephens went to the Trojans’ locker room, but only after several less-than-somber sideline exchanges with his teammates, which sparked outrage on social media. The junior from Clarkston, Michigan, is a starter for USC after making 89 tackles last season. Dylan Raiola replaced Moore, and the veteran threw a touchdown pass to Evan Stewart on his second snap to put the Ducks ahead 10-7. Raiola was a starter at Nebraska before he transferred to Oregon last January, two days before Moore made the surprising announcement of his return. Raiola decided to honor his commitment to the Ducks anyway.

articles.title: New York Jets: Jamaal Pritchett Gets His Shot
articles.summary: The Jets’ diminutive UDFA returner/receiver joins the big club
articles.body:
They show up every year at NFL camps, hoping for just one shot. One shot to show they belong in a league that has already decided they are unworthy of even a seventh round draft pick. They are the undrafted free agents, and for most of them, playing in an NFL game is just a dream.

The NFL is a tough business to break into. There are only so many roster spots available, and most are taken by draft picks. Most teams realistically have maybe three or four spots up for grab going into training camp, though injuries can open up a few more. Most years a team will bring in ten to fifteen undrafted free agents to compete in training camp, each hoping to defy the odds and secure a spot on an NFL roster. Most are destined to fail, laboring away in obscurity, ending up on practice squads, in other leagues, or out of professional football altogether. For a select few, talent, work ethic and opportunity intersect and an opening presents itself. When it does, the fortunate UDFA must seize the opportunity and immediately impress, or he is likely to have a short run in the NFL.

On Sunday an opportunity opens for the Jets' Jamaal Pritchett. A Jets UDFA originally signed in 2025, Pritchett was signed to the Jets 53 man roster on Saturday after a rash of injuries left the Jets shorthanded at wide receiver.

This isn't the first time Pritchett had to wait patiently for an opportunity. Coming out of high school the 5' 8", 175 pound receiver/returner was lightly recruited and had to walk on at South Alabama. He barely saw the field his first year, racking up just two receptions and just 62 all purpose yards. Pritchett was unfazed, working hard at his craft and getting ready for his opportunity, whenever it came.

It came quickly. In his second year in 2023 Pritchett got a chance and never looked back. Over the next two years Pritchett had 150 receptions good for 2010 yards. He was tough, shifty and explosive, and he was largely ignored on the national scene. Pritchett was overlooked in the draft process. He was a late add to the Senior Bowl, but impressed after getting his chance. He was then overlooked by all 32 NFL teams in the 2025 NFL draft before the Jets signed him as a UDFA.

Given a chance with the Jets, Pritchett again impressed, but was again overlooked. By most accounts he had an excellent training camp in 2025 and did well in the preseason games, only to be cut when the rosters had to be whittled down to 53. Pritchett latched on with the Jets practice squad but never got called up in 2025. He returned to Jets camp in 2026 and again impressed, only to again be cut again in late August. Again Pritchett was signed to the practice squad, but his chances to join the Jets 53 man roster looked bleak after the Jets broke camp with Isaiah Williams , a 2025 Pro Bowler, taking what might have been Pritchett's spot as a return man.

Sometimes all you need is a shot. Pritchett waited and worked. The football gods noticed, and an opportunity arose. The Jets' wide receiver group had multiple injuries strike over the first two games of the 2026 season. 2026 first round draft pick Omar Cooper Jr went down with an ankle injury in the first game of the season and ended up on injured reserve. 2025 fourth round draft pick Arian Smith followed him to the injured reserve list a game later, as did veteran Tim Patrick . Just like that, the Jets were severely shorthanded at receiver. Pritchett waited for the call. On Saturday, he got it.

Jamaal Pritchett had to walk on at South Alabama. He had to fight his way into the Senior Bowl after originally being snubbed. He had to wait through the NFL draft without hearing his name called. He had to sign as an undrafted free agent, play well in his limited opportunities in training camp, then get cut in late August, twice. He had to toil on the Jets practice squad and stay ready, hoping something would open up. On Saturday something opened up. He was signed to the Jets 53 man roster.

Pritchett may even get a chance on Sunday to be the Jets' primary punt returner after Isaiah Williams fumbled two punts last week. Williams had an excellent camp at wide receiver this year, and, with a depleted wide receiver group on Sunday, maybe the Jets give Wiliams a much larger role on offense and relieve him of his punt return duties, at least temporarily. No guarantees, but maybe Pritchett is back fielding punts under the bright lights in Detroit on Sunday.

For guys like Pritchett, opportunities are difficult to come by. For many no opening ever arises, and they eventually fade away after laboring in obscurity on NFL practice squads for years, replaced by the next wave of undrafted free agents hoping for just one shot. Pritchett is one of the lucky ones. On Sunday he gets his shot. Let's see what he can do with it.

articles.title: Why soccer players are sounding the alarm over NFL Brazil grass conditions
articles.summary: Here's why there are concerns at Maracana Stadium in Brazil.
articles.body:
Although the NFL continues its international series in Brazil this weekend, all eyes are on the field conditions at Maracana Stadium.

The Baltimore Ravens and Dallas Cowboys are set to face off in Rio de Janeiro in Week 3, but the grass on the field appears to be a significant concerns. In the months leading up to the game, soccer players expressed their frustration with the conditions, and that's before the NFL and the NFLPA got involved.

Still, the game continues as expected with both teams hoping to produce a key victory in the NFL season. If the conditions are poor, though, the discussion will be about why the league allowed the game to continue on in Brazil as schedule.

Here's why there are concerns at Maracana Stadium in Brazil.

In the lead-up to Sunday's Ravens-Cowboys game in Brazil, soccer players have expressed their concerns that the field conditions at Maracana Stadium are not good. Agustín Rossi, the goalie for Brazil Series A's Flamengo, bluntly said that he can't believe the soccer leagues are allowing these conditions, let alone the NFL.

"You don't even need to talk about the field, it's there for everyone to see," Augustin Rossi said to Brazilian outlet ge, via A to Z Sports . "The way we play, it's unbelievable that we're playing on a field like this. Both penalty areas are bad as (expletiuve). If you look at it, there are bumps everywhere. There's still going to be an NFL game here during the international break. After that game, I hope the field is in better shape."

Flamengo midfielder Giorgian De Arrascaeta agreed with his teammate, arguing that the field conditions continue to worsen.

"We've been struggling a lot in these last few games, and the field keeps getting worse," De Arrascaeta said. "It's getting harder and harder to control the ball. We have to try to play quickly. If we want to be champions, we have to find a solution. With the team we have, we can't be playing on a field like this."

The NFL kept the game at Maracana Stadiuma despite these concerns. In the past, the league has moved international games that didn't meet the proper standards, but apparently the league is fine with the field conditions.

However, NFLPA president JC Tretter expressed on social media his issues with the situation as Maracana Stadium continues to work on improving the field for the game.

"Our number one priority is the health and safety of our players. The concern heading into this week was that the field would be loose, patchy, and lead to excessive slipping," Tretter said. "Those conditions are generally more of a playability and performance issue than a significant injury concern.

"But safety isn't the only standard. Players should be able to perform at the level they expect of themselves and that fans expect from them. A thin, slick field may not present the same risks as a surface with too much traction, but it still affects performance and the quality of the game."

Tretter added that the field is at risk of being too slippery and unstable.

"Based on our experts' assessment, the field needed better traction and stability," he said. They recommended reinforced stitching to help the surface hold together and brought in equipment to reinforce as much of the field as possible before the game. Our experts will remain engaged and continue evaluating conditions through kickoff."

It was a clear win-now trade for a Rams team that reached last season's NFC Championship Game and has a number of impact veterans, including quarterback Matthew Stafford and wide receiver Davante Adams.

That Aaron Donald then came out of retirement to join Garrett along the defensive line only drove home the point further that Los Angeles is eyeing a Lombardi Trophy this season.

However, Donald did not play in Week 1, which means he and Garrett are yet to suit up alongside each other for a game. It seems like Rams fans may have to wait until the Week 9 game against the Washington Commanders to see that happen, which isn't until Nov. 8.

Los Angeles bounced back from its Week 1 loss with a commanding 22-point win over the New York Giants in Week 2. articles.title: Severity of Caleb Williams' Injury Revealed, New Bears Rumors on Latest Timeline to Return for QB
articles.summary: Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams is reportedly dealing with a hamstring injury that typically takes three to four weeks to heal.
articles.body:
Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams is reportedly dealing with a hamstring injury that typically takes three to four weeks to heal.

ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport reported Sunday that Williams suffered a Grade 2 hamstring injury, which doctors see as a three-to-four-week setback.

"This doesn't mean that Williams, who the Bears have touted as a quick healer, couldn't return sooner than that timeline," they explained. "It just means that doctors believe this normally is a three-to-four-week injury in most players, and that is the doctors' best estimation of how long it could take Williams to recover."

Notably, Chicago head coach Ben Johnson previously told reporters Williams is "different" than most and won't have a set timeline for his recovery.

"Here's what I know," Johnson said. "This guy's a little bit different than the average human being. I said that last night, I'll double down on that. He gets back—he has in the past—a lot faster than what people can anticipate, and so I'm not putting a timeline on this. We're going to say week-to-week. He's going to attack this with everything that he knows."

Williams had a strong start to the season when he threw for 269 yards, rushed for 65 yards and tallied four total touchdowns in a 59-37 win over the Carolina Panthers.

It was a polar opposite performance in the Bears' 9-3 Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings. Williams had just 138 yards and an interception before he exited the game halfway through the fourth quarter with the hamstring injury .

Williams, the top pick in the 2024 NFL draft, is coming off a solid second season that saw him record 3,942 yards, 27 touchdowns and seven interceptions. He added 388 rushing yards and three scores on the ground in his sophomore campaign.

Behind Williams' breakout year, the Bears finished 11-6, reaching the playoffs for the first time since 2020 and winning their first playoff game for the first time since 2010.

Williams is clearly the catalyst of Chicago's offense, and the Bears will look to get their star back on the field as soon as possible.

Unfortunately for the Bears, he isn't the only injury concern at the position.

Schefter and Rapoport noted backup Tyson Bagent was in concussion protocol Saturday but fully participated in practice. He is questionable for Monday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles.

As Patrick Mahomes gears up for Week 3 match against the Miami Dolphins after consecutive wins, he has reflected on what the team should be focusing on.Patrick Mahomes weighs in on the Kansas City Chiefs’ performance after two consecutive wins in the last weeksA few hours ago, as per Pro Football Talk, the three time Super Bowl Most Valuable Player weighed in on the new season as he said, "I think more than anything [about] who we’re playing is just staying hungry…”Patrick Mahomes added, “In this league, it’s week to week. One week they’re patting you on your back, and one week they’re telling you you’re terrible. I think all offseason we heard about how bad we were, and guys were super hungry and came in with that mentality, and I think that’s why we’ve had the success that we’ve had these first two weeks.”The Kansas City Chiefs’ popular quarterback continued, “And it’s like, how can you keep that hunger? Now everybody’s saying we’re amazing and that we’re great, and it’s like we’ve got to keep the hunger that we’ve had this entire offseason.”He added, "So that’s what we’re preaching, is like we’re nowhere near where we want to be at. We’re still so early in the season, and there’s still so much for us to learn from and so much for us to get better at, and we have to have that mentality week in and week out if we want to go out there and have success."Patrick Mahomes eyes a Super Bowl amid his impressive comeback along with Travis KelcePatrick Mahomes’ the Kansas City Chiefs is at the top of their game now as the team has recorded consecutive wins in Week 1 and 2 against the Denver Broncos and the Indianapolis Colts respectively.The team’s strongest and popular duo, Travis Kelce and Patrick Mahomes, faced a difficult time in the last few months. While the tight end was trolled for his weight gain, the quarterback was constantly doubted over his fitness levels as he trained after sustaining severe injuries in the last season.Both Travis Kelce and Patrick Mahomes have now bounced back to the field as they remain committed to winning in the new season.For now, Patrick Mahomes has thrown for a stellar 566 yards and 5 touchdowns across the Week 1 and 2 matches. articles.title: Human vs. ChatGPT NFL Week 3 betting picks: can AI recover from its ugly 2-8 start to the season?
articles.summary: GPT went 2-8 through two NFL weeks while the human sits at 5-5, setting up a pointed Week 3 betting showdown over the Bengals-Steelers spread.
articles.body: After going 0-5 in Week 1, GPT finally picked a game correctly. Actually, it picked two! But it still went under .500 and is now a dreadful 2-8 on the season. I'm exactly .500 at 5-5, which isn't awesome, but looks fantastic next to GPT's putrid 20% win rate. It also makes me feel a lot better about backing the Steelers getting 3½ points against Cincinnati in Week 3, since AI is on the opposite side. The rules remain the same. ChatGPT and I each make our five best bets using the same set of odds, and no selection can be priced worse than -120. THREE WORD GAME: THREE WORDS TO DESCRIBE EVERY NFL TEAM SO FAR THIS SEASON AHEAD OF WEEK 3 Every wager is sized to win one unit, which means a bet at -110 risks 1.10 units to win one, while a bet at +110 risks 0.91 units to win one. Odds were captured Saturday, Sept. 26, at 6 p.m. ET. Before we get to the Week 3 picks, let’s review last week. Week 2 NFL Betting Results Dan’s Week 2 NFL Betting Picks (2-3, -1.23 units) The Browns rewarded our willingness to back them after an ugly opener by beating Tampa Bay outright, while the Panthers and Falcons comfortably stayed under the total with 37 combined points. I'm going to whine about Jayden Daniels getting hurt, because that certainly didn't help our Commanders bet. But I was flat-out wrong about the Packers and Chargers. Green Bay was fortunate to win at all, and the Chargers made me look really dumb for expecting a bounce-back performance. We leaned heavily on the idea that the betting market overreacted to Week 1. Week 2 reminded us that sometimes a team looks bad because it is bad. We learned from those mistakes, and we're ready to get back on track in Week 3. GPT’s Week 2 NFL Betting Picks (2-3, -1.27 units) The robot is officially on the board! After going 0-5 in Week 1, GPT improved by going 2-3 in Week 2. Both unders cashed easily, with the Steelers and Patriots combining for 23 points and the Vikings and Bears managing just 12. The spread picks were another story. Jacksonville lost by seven, the Giants got blown out by 22 and Kansas City needed overtime to beat Indianapolis by three. GPT is now 0-7 on spread and moneyline picks through two weeks. SEASON REPORT CARD DAN: 5-5, -0.24 units GPT: 2-8, -6.50 units Dan’s Week 3 NFL Betting Card 1. New York Giants -2½ (-110) Tennessee Titans at New York Giants, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET Dan’s analysis: This is what's known as a "plug your nose" bet. It doesn't feel great to back the Giants after they just lost quarterback Jaxson Dart for the rest of the regular season and Jameis Winston looked atrocious in his stead. However, with a week preparing as the starter, I expect Winston to be better and the Giants to rally around their backup QB. Plus, I just don't think Tennessee is very good. GPT’s analysis: Getting the Giants below a field goal is the appeal, and Malik Nabers being cleared gives Jameis Winston his most important receiving option. My concern is trusting New York to create separation with a replacement quarterback on a short week. Brian Burns, Deonte Banks and Tyler Nubin are questionable, while Tennessee’s running game offers a way to keep this close. I passed because the Giants’ defensive uncertainty outweighs the attractive number. 2. Pittsburgh Steelers +3½ (-112) Cincinnati Bengals at Pittsburgh Steelers, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET Dan’s analysis: This is definitely a "fade the public" type bet. The Steelers haven't looked good in either of their two games, despite being 1-1, and the Bengals look like legitimate Super Bowl contenders. So, why are we backing Pittsburgh? I love getting 3½ points at home in a divisional matchup. With everyone expecting Cincinnati to roll Pittsburgh, I'll grab the points. GPT’s analysis: The extra half-point is valuable in a matchup Pittsburgh’s defense could turn into a field-goal game. This is our direct head-to-head disagreement, though. I’m backing Cincinnati because its improved defensive front faces a struggling Steelers offense, while Joey Porter Jr. and Jamel Dean are questionable against Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Pittsburgh can cover without winning, but I trust Cincinnati’s paths to creating a margin more. 3. Tampa Bay Buccaneers Moneyline (+106) Minnesota Vikings at Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Sunday at 4:05 p.m. ET Dan’s analysis: Honestly, the Vikings have been at their best with Kyler Murray not playing quarterback, and he's back to starting in Week 3. This just feels like the Vikings are a pretty fraudulent 2-0 and the Bucs are probably not quite as bad as their 0-2 record suggests. The lookahead line prior to Week 2 favored the Bucs, so I think we're getting a lot of value with Tampa as a home dog. GPT’s analysis: There is a reasonable case for looking past Minnesota’s 2-0 record and Tampa Bay’s 0-2 start. The Vikings have not consistently sustained offense, and Tampa Bay has left scoring opportunities unfinished. I also prefer the Buccaneers moneyline to taking just one point. What keeps me off the bet is Baker Mayfield’s protection matchup against Brian Flores’ pressure, plus the uncertainty of projecting Minnesota’s offense with Kyler Murray returning. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER 4. Las Vegas Raiders-New Orleans Saints Over 44 (-105) Las Vegas Raiders at New Orleans Saints, Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET Dan’s analysis: This game has sneaky shootout potential, especially with the suddenly explosive Saints' offense led by Tyler Shough and Chris Olave. Entering Week 3, Shough led the NFL in passing yards, while Olave ranked second in receiving yards. The potential return of Brock Bowers would boost a Raiders' offense that has quietly produced 53 points through two weeks despite missing its best offensive weapon. GPT’s analysis: Tyler Shough and Chris Olave give this over a credible explosive-play argument, and a Brock Bowers return could raise Las Vegas’ offensive ceiling. Bowers remains questionable, however, and the Raiders have preferred long possessions while struggling to generate consistent yardage. Their pass rush also faces a Saints line missing left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. I’m backing Las Vegas +3, but I’m less confident these offenses combine for at least 45 points. 5. Philadelphia Eagles-Chicago Bears Under 42½ (-110) Philadelphia Eagles at Chicago Bears, Monday at 8:15 p.m. ET Dan’s analysis: Following a historic Week 1 offensive performance, Chicago couldn't back it up in Week 2 and scored just 3 points against the Vikings. With Caleb Williams set to miss the game and backup quarterback Tyson Bagent also questionable, it's hard to see how the Bears score more than 17 points against Philadelphia. On the other hand, the Eagles' offense hasn't been very good, either. Finally, primetime unders have been profitable since the start of 2016. Caleb Williams is out, Chicago has not confirmed whether Tyson Bagent or Case Keenum will start, and Philadelphia is missing Dallas Goedert. Those absences support a lower-scoring game. My hesitation is that Chicago can still attack Philadelphia’s vulnerable run defense, while Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith are cleared. I lean under, but the quarterback downgrade is already reflected in the number. Explain exactly why you’re selecting each of the five bets. Also explain exactly why you’re passing on the eligible bets you don’t select. Use at least 10 different sources for each game so you have a broad understanding of everything surrounding each game. Before delivering the results, do a fact-check and ensure that everything is correct." After nearly 30 minutes of thinking, here’s what it came up with. 1. Buffalo Bills -7 (-112) Los Angeles Chargers at Buffalo Bills, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET GPT’s analysis: Buffalo has scored 77 points through two games, while the Chargers have managed 14 in each of theirs. The Bills also have additional preparation time after playing Thursday in Week 2. Los Angeles’ protection problems and confirmed absences on defense give Buffalo several ways to build a lead. DJ Moore and Keon Coleman being questionable is the main concern, but I still favor Buffalo at a number that pushes on a touchdown win. GPT’s projected score: Bills 30, Chargers 20 Dan’s analysis: This feels like a trap. Buffalo should wipe the floor with the hapless Chargers, but that's exactly why I wouldn't go anywhere near this spread. Bets that seem obvious usually aren't. ROB GRONKOWSKI CALLS CHARGERS 'PROBABLY THE BIGGEST MESS IN THE NFL' RIGHT NOW AFTER ROUGH START 2. Jacksonville Jaguars -3 (+100) New England Patriots at Jacksonville Jaguars, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET GPT’s analysis: Jacksonville’s defensive front can exploit New England’s protection after Mike Onwenu’s move to injured reserve. The Patriots are also missing edge players Dre’Mont Jones and Quintayvious Hutchins, making it harder to pressure Trevor Lawrence without additional help. New England’s defense remains the strongest counterargument, particularly after Jacksonville struggled in Denver. At even money, though, I’m willing to back the Jaguars with a push on a three-point victory. GPT’s projected score: Jaguars 24, Patriots 20 Dan’s analysis: I like this look because one would think the public would love getting the Patriots as a dog in this spot. Cincinnati Bengals -3½ (-104) Cincinnati Bengals at Pittsburgh Steelers, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET GPT’s analysis: Cincinnati’s rebuilt defense has eight sacks through two games and just held Houston without a touchdown. Pittsburgh comes off a three-point performance and has uncertainty at receiver, running back and both outside cornerback spots. Those questionable players could play, but Burrow, Chase and Higgins give Cincinnati the more dependable passing combination. Laying more than a field goal is the risk; the relatively inexpensive -104 price helps make it worthwhile. GPT’s projected score: Bengals 24, Steelers 17 Dan’s analysis: Well, I bet the Steelers, so you can probably guess that I don't like this pick. 4. At +102, a narrow Saints win can still cash the bet, and a three-point Raiders loss returns the stake. GPT’s projected score: Saints 23, Raiders 21 Dan’s analysis: I don't love this one, either. Davante Adams and Jaylen Waddle create explosive-play risk, and 44 offers less cushion than the earlier 45½. I still favor the under, with exactly 44 returning the stake.
