articles.title: Goodell Addresses Concerns over Grass Field, Travel, QB Injuries Before Ravens vs. Cowboys in Brazil
articles.summary: NFL commissioner Roger Goodell addressed a number of topics about the 2026 season during a sit-down interview with ESPN's Stephen A. Smith, including the league's decision to play Sunday's Week 3 game between the Dallas Cowboys and Baltimore Ravens in Brazil.
articles.body:
NFL commissioner Roger Goodell addressed a number of topics about the 2026 season during a sit-down interview with ESPN's Stephen A. Smith, including the league's decision to play Sunday's Week 3 game between the Dallas Cowboys and Baltimore Ravens in Brazil.

The field conditions Maracanã Stadium have been a particular talking point after National Football League Players Association executive director JC Tretter raised concerns on social media.

"The complaints that you've heard were for the soccer players that were playing on the field," Goodell said (2:55 mark). "They have a different barometer, a different standard. Theirs is about the ball rolling smoothly on a grass field. That's not what our issue is. Our issue is stability and proper footing. And they are two different things. We saw that in the World Cup."

He also said the league has worked with the NFLPA to make more consistent playing surfaces across the league, whether fields be grass or turf.

Still, Tretter addressed the Brazil game and said "based on our experts' assessment, the field needed better traction and stability.

"... The NFL has been clear they want to continue to grow the game internationally. However, growth alone cannot be the goal. The goal has to be growing the game while maintaining the standards our players deserve. If we can't do both, then we need to make different decisions."

Sunday's game will already be the second international one of the season, as the San Francisco 49ers and Los Angeles Rams started the campaign in Australia.

Goodell also addressed travel concerns both leading up to and after the international games.

"We're looking for input. What are the important things? When we were in Australia a couple of weeks ago, we spent a lot of time talking about that," he said (4:17 mark). "… So all of this is something you're learning as we go and you're trying to understand what's the best way to prepare for the game and the best way to recover, which is a big factor. We've played in Brazil before, this is our third year.

"… We're learning more. When we play in Europe, a lot of times the teams from the West Coast play on the East Coast and then go over. I think we've been able to do that effectively, but you can always get better at it."

Both the Rams and 49ers won their Week 2 games after the Australia trip, although Los Angeles' victory over the New York Giants was largely defined by Jaxson Dart's injury.

His setback was one of a handful of injuries for quarterbacks through the first two weeks, as Caleb Williams, Jayden Daniels and Sam Darnold have also been sidelined.

"You never like to see that," Goodell said (9:43 mark). "This is one of the reasons we focus so much on player safety. You want those guys, and they want to be out there to compete. … We probably get a lot of criticism that we protect the quarterbacks too much.

"But I think there's a dynamic there where the players are in defenseless positions, and that's been our focus whether you're a quarterback or a receiver or any other position, that's the area that we've always focused on. What do you do to make sure they're protected?"

He explained he believes quarterbacks can better understand when they are running they lose many of those protections granted to them in the pocket.

Still, injuries have been a defining storyline in the early going this season, as a number of high-profile teams are already turning to their backups.

Baltimore and Dallas will both have their starters in Lamar Jackson and Dak Prescott available Sunday, but the playing surface figures to be a talking point leading up to and throughout the contest.

articles.title: New Giants Rumors on Jimmy G, Fields, Mac Jones Joining J.J. McCarthy as QBs Eyed After Dart Injury
articles.summary: While Jameis Winston could secure his starting spot moving forward with an impressive showing in Sunday's game against the Tennessee Titans, the New York Giants are reportedly looking at a number of quarterbacks with Jaxson Dart sidelined for the remainder of the campaign with a knee injury.
articles.body:
While Jameis Winston could secure his starting spot moving forward with an impressive showing in Sunday's game against the Tennessee Titans, the New York Giants are reportedly looking at a number of quarterbacks with Jaxson Dart sidelined for the remainder of the campaign with a knee injury.

ESPN's Ian Rapoport, Adam Schefter and Mike Garafolo reported Sunday the list of potential targets includes free agent Jimmy Garoppolo, Minnesota Vikings third-stringer J.J. McCarthy, San Francisco 49ers backup Mac Jones, Kansas City Chiefs backup Justin Fields, Arizona Cardinals backup Gardner Minshew II and Brandon Allen, who was in training camp with New York.

This comes after Tom Pelissero of The Ringer reported Saturday "it's a matter of when, not if, the Giants add another passer with starting experience, potentially as soon as Monday."

Pelissero listed McCarthy as someone who was "intriguing" as a potential option for the NFC East team.

The quarterback situation will loom over the matchup with the Titans, especially since Winston struggled during the team's Week 2 loss to the Los Angeles Rams when he entered for Dart.

He went 11-of-27 for 111 yards, zero touchdowns and one interception, although he was unexpectedly thrown into action as a pocket passer after the game plan was built around the more mobile Dart.

The veteran had time to better prepare for Sunday's game, and the ESPN report noted "how hard the Giants push to acquire a veteran quarterback will be determined, in part, by how Winston performs."

As for the other options, Pelissero highlighted how the Giants scouted McCarthy before the Vikings selected him with the No. 10 pick of the 2024 NFL draft. He also played at Michigan for Jim Harbaugh, who is the brother of New York head coach John Harbaugh.

That he is Minnesota's third-stringer makes him more expendable as well, although he is that far on the depth chart for a reason after struggling throughout the 2025 campaign with 11 touchdown passes to 12 interceptions.

There are connections in place with the other options as well.

Minshew and Fields have both played for Giants offensive coordinator Matt Nagy in the past, while Garoppolo has held discussions with New York as he remains unsigned, per ESPN. As a free agent, he also wouldn't require giving something up in a trade like the others.

Then there is Jones, who impressed last season while going 5-3 as a starter when Brock Purdy was sidelined in San Francisco.

Still, that performance underscored the importance of having a quality backup for contenders. The 49ers made the playoffs in part because of his individual play, and there could be some hesitance from teams to give up their backups with that as the backdrop.

That could also drive up the asking price in any discussions with the Giants, who are exploring a number of different options.

articles.title: NFL told Azeez Al-Shaair he'd be pulled from Texans game over pro-Palestinian eyeblack message
articles.summary: Azeez Al-Shaair wore pro-Palestinian eyeblack again in Week 2 against the Cincinnati Bengals but was told he'd be removed from the Houston Texans game.
articles.body: Azeez Al-Shaair tried for the second consecutive week to mark his eyeblack with an anti-Israel and pro-Palestinian message last week, but backed down when an NFL official told him he'd be removed from the game if he persisted, an NFL source told OutKick. Al-Shaair, a linebacker for the Houston Texans, was fined $11,492 in Week 1 when he inscribed the name of slain Palestinian girl Hind Rajab on his eyeblack to highlight her death during a bombing in Gaza by the Israeli Defense Force. The NFL prohibits the display of personal messages by players throughout game day. NFL FINES PLAYER NICKNAMED 'JUICE' $14,926 FOR USING A DRINKING CELEBRATION, CALLING IT OFFENSIVE Al-Shaair, who is Muslim, was undeterred by the cost of the Week 1 fine because he came out for warmups before the Week 2 game against the Cincinnati Bengals wearing the name of another Palestinian girl – Wafaa Akila – on his eyeblack. The eyeblack inscription remained even when the game began but then an NFL official spotted it, according to the league source, and informed the Texans and Al-Shaair he must remove it or he'd be removed from the game altogether. NEW NFL FINE SCHEDULE IS GOING TO A POINT SYSTEM THAT COULD LEAD TO SUSPENSIONS BUT ALSO REFUNDS The threat of not being able to play apparently convinced Al-Shaair to do something the threat of being fined again obviously did not. He removed the eyeblack and played the entire rest of the game without any eyeblack. The threat of fines is not important to Al-Shaair. He signed a three-year contract extension worth $54 million in April. He also did not appeal last week's fine. NBA STAR KYRIE IRVING JUMPS INTO NFL DRAMA, OFFERS TO PAY PLAYER'S FINE FOR GAZA-THEMED EYE BLACK "What’s a life worth?" Al-Shaair told reporters last week when questioned about the fine and his anti-Israel campaign. "Is a life worth $11,000? I think it’s priceless. So, to sit there and say that, ‘Oh man, the money’ and whatever, that wasn’t relevant to me." PRO-PALESTINE PROTESTER WHO INTERRUPTED SUPER BOWL LIX HALFTIME SHOW FOUND GUILTY IN COURT But playing time obviously is relevant to Al-Shaair, who is now basically on the NFL's radar for repeatedly trying to amplify pro-Palestine and anti-Israeli messages on game days. In January, the linebacker was fined $11,593 for wearing eyeblack on which he inscribed the slogan "Stop the Genocide." So is the NFL cracking down on Al-Shaair personally? No. The league has a long history of not allowing players to share personal messaging. And it has a long history of cautioning players that if they persist, they will be removed from games. Chicago Bears quarterback Jim McMahon was told prior to Super Bowl XX in 1986 that he must abstain from wearing a headband with messages or would not be allowed to play. Maxx Crosby, Odell Beckham and A.J. Brown have been told during various times they must change out of personalized cleats or be removed from a game. Last week, Arizona Cardinals defensive back Kei'Trel Clark was fined when he inscribed his eyeblack with the message "Glory B 2 God." NFL RESTARTS SOCIAL JUSTICE SLOGANS ON FIELDS WHILE ITS BATTLING DRUNK DRIVING, DOMESTIC ABUSE, PROSTITUTION ARREST OFF THE FIELD Why does the NFL have this policy when it actually inscribes messages on its fields every game day? Simple: The league wants to maintain consistency in how its teams and players look and avoid, as one source put it, "the wild west out there." That is clearly the right approach. If the NFL allowed players to express their individualism by marking up their uniforms, helmets, eyeblack, cleats, or themselves, it's impossible to predict in what direction those personalized messages would go. Al-Shaair is an example of that. He is not an honest broker about what is happening in Gaza or in the Hamas-Israel conflict. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! He has a certain worldview about the Middle East and that's what he's trying to amplify on the NFL stage. He has highlighted, what is in the case of Rajab, the death of an innocent Palestinian girl. But he has never mentioned the death of all the innocent Israeli boys and girls that preceded it on Oct. 7, 2023. And he has never mentioned the way Hamas uses children as shields, couriers, and even as weapons transporters while the IDF holds fire. The Houston Texans play visit the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. The NFL will be watching. FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

articles.title: Arch Manning 'Looks More Like a Player Who Could' Skip 2027 NFL Draft, Return to Texas, Says Brugler
articles.summary: Arch Manning's performance through four games of his second season starting for Texas has at least one analyst wondering if he will be back for a third.
articles.body:
Arch Manning's performance through four games of his second season starting for Texas has at least one analyst wondering if he will be back for a third.

The Athletic's Dane Brugler noted Saturday "it is still very early, and a lot can change over the next three months."

"Through four games, however, Manning looks more like a player who could go back to school for a fifth season rather than be taken No. 1 overall in April," Brugler reported.

B/R NFL scouts ranked Manning on their latest 2027 NFL Draft Big Board as the No. 17 overall prospect and No. 4 quarterback behind Miami's Darian Mensah, Oregon's Dante Moore and Ole Miss' Trinidad Chambliss.

Brugler's report followed a 20-17 win over Tennessee in which Texas leaned on star pass rusher Colin Simmons tying a single-game program record with five sacks to make up for struggles from the Volunteers' offense.

Manning, who went into this season looking to take a step forward from an inconsistent first starting campaign, threw an interception and went three-and-out on six of 12 offensive drives.

Manning has completed 63.5 percent of his passes for 862 yards with seven touchdowns and three picks while taking 10 sacks during the Longhorns' 4-0 start to the season.

He has at times seemingly struggled to operate Steve Sarkisian's offense, which he has been working since his first season as backup to Quinn Ewers in 2023.

ESPN's Jordan Reid noted after the game Manning "locks onto targets and doesn't always read" defensive setups like the Tennessee double coverage he threw into for Saturday's second-quarter interception.

"Being that this is Year 4 in Sark's offense, you'd hope the developmental curve and IQ situations would be further along, but they just aren't early on in the season," Reid reported.

Multiple teams are likely to be heading into the 2027 NFL draft with immediate needs at quarterback, including the Pittsburgh Steelers, Cleveland Browns, New York Jets, Indianapolis Colts, Arizona Cardinals and Miami Dolphins.

It seems likely one of these teams could be willing to take a chance on Manning should he decide to enter the 2027 draft. If he wants to be selected with the No. 1 pick, however, he may need to put together some stronger performances down the stretch of the Longhorns' season.

articles.title: Giants reportedly considering Jimmy Garoppolo, Vikings' J.J. McCarthy, 49ers' Mac Jones to potentially fill QB role in wake of Jaxson Dart's injury
articles.summary: Jameis Winston will start in Week 3.
articles.body:
As Jameis Winston starts in place of injured quarterback Jaxson Dart for the New York Giants in Week 3 against the Tennessee Titans , the team continues to look at other potential options for the position.

ESPN and NFL Network reported a handful of quarterbacks the Giants could consider bringing in based on their evaluation of Winston's performance:

The Giants elevated Jake Haener from their practice squad to be Winston's backup in Week 3.

Giants coach John Harbaugh has said the team is looking at all options to fill the position after Dart was lost to a knee injury that will sideline him for at least the remainder of the regular season.

Winston's performance against the Titans could determine how aggressively the Giants decide to pursue another experienced quarterback, ESPN reported. Winston struggled after he replaced Dart early in the Giants' Week 2 loss to the Los Angeles Rams , but New York reportedly thinks he will play better now that the coaches will build a game plan more suited to his skills.

McCarthy has fallen to third on Minnesota 's depth chart after starting some of last season. It is unclear if the Cardinals, 49ers or Chiefs will consider parting with their backups given the number of injuries starting quarterbacks have suffered already this season.

articles.title: New NFL Rumors on Justin Herbert in Mike McDaniel's 'Incredibly Complex' Offense amid Chargers' Woes
articles.summary: NFL Network's Ian Rapoport feels the Los Angeles Chargers' 0-2 start to the season is in part because quarterback Justin Herbert is still adapting to working with his new offensive coordinator.
articles.body:
NFL Network's Ian Rapoport feels the Los Angeles Chargers' 0-2 start to the season is in part because quarterback Justin Herbert is still adapting to working with his new offensive coordinator.

"Mike McDaniel's offense— My understanding is, it's incredibly complex, probably more complex than people realize, which may explain why Justin Herbert has not looked like themselves," Rapoport said Sunday on NFL Game Day Morning.

"What they'd like to do... is get Herbert to just take the check down from time to time."

After opening the season with losses to the Arizona Cardinals and Las Vegas Raiders, the Chargers are looking to bounce back Sunday with a 1 p.m. ET matchup at the Buffalo Bills.

Herbert has completed less than 60 percent of his passes while throwing for 401 yards with two touchdowns and three interceptions over that span.

He hasn't been the only member of the Chargers offense struggling. After seven penalties and two turnovers in a season-opening loss to the Cardinals, the Bolts fumbled six times and took eight penalties against the Raiders.

"We've got some growing pains," head coach Jim Harbaugh said the day after the Week 2 loss.

The Chargers hired McDaniel this offseason after he was fired as head coach of the Miami Dolphins, a team that ranked among the NFL's top offenses during McDaniel's first two years with the program in 2022 and 2023.

When asked earlier this week if he was considering simplifying his offense ahead of Week 3 with his new team, McDaniel acknowledged he was but added he was trying not to "overreact."

"My expectation would be we'd be building a foundation for the best play in December, and elimination football," McDaniel said .

About working with Herbert, McDaniel said the circumstances of the Chargers' 0-2 start "have forced our hand into a lot of tape and conversations that I'm much closer to him now than I was two weeks ago."

"Two games in, I have a better idea of what guys are comfortable with right now," McDaniel said.

The Chargers will now hope that experience will allow McDaniel to help Herbert and the rest of his offense take advantage of a Week 3 matchup against a Bills defense that ranks 30th in passing yards allowed through two games.

articles.title: Missouri State falls to SMU, but Casey Woods says Bears proved they can compete with top programs
articles.summary: Missouri State fell to SMU 34-24 but coach Casey Woods believes the team proved it can compete with top programs.
articles.body:
See our best photos from Missouri State football at SMU in Week 4

DALLAS —The underdogs had a fighting chance late.

Missouri State pulled a possession in the fourth quarter, but gave up two touchdowns in a 1-minute, 27-second span and lost 34-24 at Gerald J. Ford Stadium.

The Bears pulled within 21-16 following a touchdown pass from Skyler Locklear to Isaiah Myers with 12:16 left against No. 22-ranked SMU .

Locklear threw an incomplete pass on the 2-point conversion, but a pass interference call on the Mustangs gave the Bears another chance. Locklear capitalized on a 1-yard run, and the Bears pulled within 21-18.

Then, the Bears defense forced a 3-and-out.

That play dropped SMU's win probability from 99.3% to 86.2% on ESPN's analytics.

Missouri State would get the ball with a chance to tie or take the lead on the road against a Power 4 program.

"You know, that's what you pray for going in these games," Locklear said. "Have a chance to go win it."

On 3rd-and-4, the Bears went for the home run ball and missed. Incomplete pass.

Six plays later, Heisman Trophy candidate Kevin Jennings threw a touchdown pass to give the Mustangs some breathing room. A Bears' turnover on the next drive, an interception, led to another SMU touchdown and a 34-18 deficit, which all but sealed their fate.

The Bears lost by 10 to a team that was favored to win by 34.5 points according to many betting sites.

"We didn't get it done, but you know, credit to our defense, credit to special teams, credit to the offensive line, the receivers," Locklear said. "You know, everybody played their hearts out and fought to the very end."

Missouri State flew back to Springfield with a 1-3 mark after non-conference games with losses to Marshall , Texas A&M and SMU.

However, you have to walk before you can run.

While moral victories only count to fans, first-year head coach Casey Woods saw that his team can hang with a talented team like SMU.

"You saw us tonight," Woods said. "We're capable of competing at a level with a really, really, really good football team."

It was not long after Woods was hired to coach at SMU — in 2022 — that the Mustangs turned the corner from being a good team to being a Top 25-ranked program.

The Mustangs were in the American Conference in 2022 and went 7-6 that season — after a 2-3 start.

The next year, SMU went 11-3 and won the American Conference championship. Two years after that, in the ACC, the Mustangs made the college football playoffs.

Woods returned to The Hilltop on Saturday as an opposing coach, but the memories he built with Rhett Lashlee could be the foundation that could continue the Bears' trajectory as an FBS program. He asked what it meant to be back in Dallas.

"Here's what I think about… the greatest memories that I've got are really an encouragement to what it is that we want to do at Missouri State," he said. "And what it is that we want to do at Springfield."

SMU didn't have much tradition after Eric Dickerson. There were some bowl game trips, but generally, even in the good years, the Mustangs were barely .500.

The same Kevin Jennings that torched the Bears for 464 yards on Saturday night was the same Kevin Jennings from nearby Dallas South Oak Cliff that flipped his commitment from Missouri State to SMU. The Gary Webber End Zone Complex was proposed: a $100 million complex that connected the stadium's east and west gates and turned a hill into a state-of-the-art facility with a new weight room, locker room, players' lounge, and sports medicine center for the football players. The second floor had an on-site kitchen to make meals for the 17 varsity programs. The third floor had premium lounge spaces for boosters.

"The end zone was a hill, and the students weren't coming to the games," Woods said. "It was four years ago. So we're not talking about 100 years of tradition. We built the facility just like we're building the facility (in Springfield). We went and sold it to the student body just like we're selling to the student body. We went and sold it to the community. The community got their ass off of the boulevard and came in and started watching the games."

Woods sees the parallels between what happened at SMU and what he wants to happen at MSU.

He just needs to dig up the horse bones, or Bear bones if you will, move them and keep building.

When the end zone football complex was underway, construction crews found the bones of the original Peruna and the other Shetland ponies that followed as the mascot for the Mustangs. When each of the Perunas passed, it was buried in the 'hill' that sat beyond the end zone in what was a U-shaped stadium.

"We moved the horse bones, we got them in a great place and we built this facility and then went to win two conference championships and everybody's like, 'man, that's probably a smart move to move the horse bones, right?' So we've got a chance to do that. We have our own horse bones at Missouri State and in Springfield. For every single person that steps in the stadium is like, 'Ah, same old Missouri State that's always been.' That's the attitude we got to change, right?" No, this has got to be like, you're missing out.

This was a hell of a crowd. We got to get our asses in the seats and make sure we fill the stadium, so we can give to this university that's going to give back to Springfield and make sure that we do that right. That's what I mean by it takes all of us. It's everybody's role."

articles.title: QB Drew Sheridan sees system fit, special atmosphere at Pitt
articles.summary: Pittsburgh had Dearborn (Mich.) Divine Child quarrterback Drew Sheridan on campus for an unofficial visit on Saturday. The junior signal-caller saw the Panth...
articles.body:
Pittsburgh had Dearborn (Mich.) Divine Child quarrterback Drew Sheridan on campus for an unofficial visit on Saturday. The junior signal-caller saw the Panthers defeat Bucknell.

He had been to campus in the past, but this gameday visit allowed him a different experience than his previous trips.

"Game day there is something special that I never realized until now," Sheridan said. "I'm excited about Pitt and I'm excited about the culture Coach Narduzzi has built there."

Pitt has had a good history of quarterback development and Sheridan sees a potential fit in the way they play. To date, Sheridan has been extremely efficient this season. He is completing over 80 percent of his passes and has thrown no interceptions.

"Watching their offense, which throws the ball 70 percent of the time, is extremely cerebral and quarterback driven: RPOs , lots of reads, attacking the middle of the field and utilizing big tight ends. Those are things that are all at the top of my skill set as a quarterback. The more I watch Pitt, the more I can see myself playing there."

Pitt was an earlier offer for Sheridan. They have steadily recruited him. However, the contact has increased of late, and as the 2028 quarterback recruiting picture continues to develop nationally, the Panthers have made their interest in him clear.

"My relationship with multiple coaches and admin has grown a lot, I'd say over the last month, month and a half," Sheridan said. "I communicate multiple times a week with them. The biggest thing for me is that they cut up my game films every week and really know what I'm doing on a week to week basis. I look forward to continuing the process with Pitt, and I also can see myself playing there in the future."

Sheridan is a three-star prospect per Rivals. He helped his team win a state title as a sophomore and has them undefeated thus far as a junior. He has been a varsity starter since his freshman season.

Kentucky and Rutgers are two schools he visited this season. He is working on a date to get to Michigan also.
